subject: A/B stabilization: promptset regression handoff & acceptance asks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-14T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: A/B stabilization: promptset regression handoff & acceptance asks

Hi team,

Quick sync: AtlasHealth flagged recurring quality regressions in their promptset AB run (see Emily cc'd). We're handing this from discovery into a stabilization plan and I want to lock acceptance criteria + owners by EOD tomorrow so we can start a focused fix sprint next week. High-level asks below — please reply with concrete owners or corrections.

1) Acceptance criteria (min):
  - Automated eval pass rate >= 92% on the core safety and medical-accuracy suites (EVAL-4321).
  - No user-visible hallucination regressions in the top-50 customer flows (sampled).
  - Latency delta <= 10% of current baseline for the candidate quantized model.

2) A/B rollout plan constraints:
  - Canary at 1% for 24h, 5% for 48h, then ramp if metrics stable (we can tweak).
  - Immediate rollback triggers: >3% degradation in acceptance pass or any P1 user report.

3) Required deliverables before canary:
  - Regression repro promptset + seed list (Priyom).
  - Test harness job and metrics dashboard (Karthik).
  - Product sign-off on acceptance thresholds (Grace).

4) Timeline preference: aim to have canary by 9/20 if engineering capacity permits.

Emily, thanks for surfacing this — if you can confirm any additional customer tolerances (e.g., if the latency cap needs to be tighter) that'd be helpful.

I'll attach the stabilization checklist and the latest eval playbook.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior PM, Evals & Safeguards
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: A/B stabilization: promptset regression handoff & acceptance asks

Thanks Marissa — tagging some specifics from an engineering/ops perspective.

Quick answers: I can own the test harness and dashboard (Karthik). Priyom, can you drop the repro promptset into the shared drive by EOD? That's the dependency to start.

Acceptance items (engineering detail):
- "Automated eval pass rate >= 92%": we need to lock which metrics compose the pass rate (precision/recall/credibility). Proposal: weighted score (70% accuracy/30% safety). I'll add this to JIRA EVAL-4321.
- Latency cap: we can guarantee latency delta <= 10% on our dedicated infra if we don't switch to a different quantization path. If we need a tighter cap we should run a short perf trial against the candidate quant build.

Test plan deliverables:
- Regression harness job (k8s CronJob) + artifacts: gold prompts, gold assertions, and a token-level diff report.
- Dashboard widgets: pass rate, per-flow hallucination count, median latency, and top-10 failing prompts.

Open question for product: how strict do you want to be on per-flow drift vs aggregate? For AtlasHealth we probably need per-flow guarantees on the top-10 flows; otherwise a single noisy flow can hide broad regressions.

I'll create the EVAL-4321 subtask list today.

—Karthik
Principal Engineer, Inference Tools
Redwood Inference

Appreciate the clear framing, Marissa. From product/CS side:

- Confirming AtlasHealth tolerance: Emily, for clinical flows we need accuracy >= 94% ideally; if that isn't realistic we can accept 92% with an explicit list of "guarded flows" where we require human review. Can you confirm?

- Per-flow guarantees: I agree with Karthik — top-10 flows need independent thresholds. We'll provide a prioritized list by EOD tomorrow.

- Rollout policy: can we add a soft-hold stage (5% but traffic only from internal beta users + Atlas test tenants) for 48h before broader 5% exposure? That reduces blast radius.

Owners: Product sign-off owner is Grace O'Connor. I'll validate acceptance thresholds and the prioritized flows.

Grace
Product Lead, Assistant Experiences
Redwood Inference

Looping in operational constraints — I can run the canary and monitor SLIs. A few practical notes: 

- Canary cadence: I like Grace's soft-hold. Proposed schedule: 1% internal-only (12h) -> 1% Atlas test tenants (36h) -> 5% mixed (48h) -> 10% if stable.
- Monitoring: I will add a smoke alert for any hallucination increase >1 absolute point and a separate alert for pass-rate drop >2 points across the golden suite. Both will auto-pause routing to the candidate model.
- Rollback runbook: I updated the runbook with explicit rollback steps and contact list; link below.

Link: https://docs.redwood.ai/shared/ab-stabilization-runbook

I can be on-call during the canary window. If Emily or Atlas prefers to do their own traffic slice for validation, we can coordinate that in the run.

—Sean

Redwood Inference
